thought_title: The heavenly garment must be acquired now
orientation: Macarius is exhorting his hearers to strive now through faith and virtuous conduct to possess the heavenly garment, so that at the resurrection their bodies will not be found naked.
pass_a_gloss: Let us strive therefore through faith and virtuous conduct to acquire from here that garment, so that, having put on the body, we may not be found naked, and there is nothing that will glorify our flesh on that day. For each one, as much as he was deemed worthy through faith and zeal to become a partaker of the Holy Spirit, to that extent on that day his body also will be glorified. For what the soul has now stored up within, then will be uncovered and will appear outside the body. Just as the trees, having passed through the winter, when an invisible power warms them from within, from the sun and the winds, put forth and cast out leaves like garments, and flowers, and fruits, likewise the flowers of the grass in that season come forth from within from the bosoms of the earth, and the earth is covered and clothed, and the grass is like the lilies, about which the Lord said: That not even Solomon in all his glory was arrayed like one of these. For all these things are examples, and types, and images of the Christians. So for all God-loving souls, that is, for true Christians, there is the first month Xanthicus, the one called April, which is the day of the resurrection, and through the power of the sun of righteousness from within comes forth the glory of the Holy Spirit, covering and sheltering the bodies of the saints, which glory they had hidden within in their souls. For what it has now, that very thing comes forth outside the body then. This, I say, is the first month among the months of the year; this brings joy to all creation; this clothes the naked trees, opening the earth; this brings joy to all the animals; this shows cheerfulness to all; this is for Christians the first month, Xanthicus, which is the season of the resurrection, in which their bodies will be glorified, through the ineffable light that is in them from now, that is, the power of the Spirit, which will be to them then garment, food, drink, exultation, joy, peace, clothing, eternal life; for all beauty of brightness and of heavenly loveliness, the Spirit of the Godhead becomes for them then. Just as therefore each of us ought to believe, and to strive, and to be zealous, and to conduct himself well, and to love the Lord, and to be filled with the Holy Spirit, so that we may be found worthy of the eternal good things.

choices.why: The adverb means 'from this place' or 'from now,' emphasizing that the garment must be acquired in this present life before the resurrection.
The middle participle of ἐνδύω with the body as object means the soul is clothed with the body at the resurrection; the image is of the body as a garment that must not be found naked.
rejected: when we put on the body

choices.why: The compound verb with the prefix ἐν- emphasizes the inward location of the treasure in the soul, matching the author's contrast between hidden inner glory and its outward manifestation.
The plural 'bosoms' is a literal rendering of the Greek, preserving the image of the earth's interior as a womb from which the flowers emerge.
The passive of ἀμφιέννυμι means to be wrapped or clothed around, fitting the garment imagery that runs through the passage.
ἱλαρότης means gladness or cheerfulness, a quality of brightness and joy that the spring month displays to all.

pass_b_english: Let us strive, then, through faith and virtuous conduct to acquire that garment from here, so that, having clothed the body, we may not be found naked, and there may be nothing to glorify our flesh on that day. For each person, to the degree that he was deemed worthy through faith and diligence to become a partaker of the Holy Spirit, to that same degree his body also will be glorified on that day. What the soul has stored up within now will then be uncovered and appear outside the body.

Just as the trees, when winter has passed and an invisible power from the sun and the winds warms them from within, put forth and send out leaves like garments, and flowers, and fruits—so too the flowers of the grass in that season come forth from within the earth, and the earth is covered and clothed, and the grass is like the lilies, about which the Lord said, “Not even Solomon in all his glory was arrayed like one of these” (Matthew 6:29; Luke 12:27). For all these things are examples, and types, and images of the things to come.

So for all God-loving souls—that is, for true Christians—the first month is the month called April, which is the day of the resurrection. And through the power of the sun of righteousness, the glory of the Holy Spirit comes forth from within, covering and sheltering the bodies of the saints—that glory which they had hidden within their souls. For what a person has now, that same thing comes forth outside the body then.

This month, I say, is the first of the months of the year. This month brings joy to all creation. This month clothes the naked trees and opens the earth. This month brings joy to all living creatures. This month displays cheerfulness to all. This is the first month for Christians—the month called April, which is the season of the resurrection, in which their bodies will be glorified through the ineffable light that is in them even now, that is, through the power of the Holy Spirit. That Spirit will then be to them garment, food, drink, exultation, joy, peace, and eternal life. For all the beauty of heavenly brightness and loveliness the Spirit of the Godhead will then become theirs.
Therefore each of us ought to believe and strive.

problems.quote: when we have put on the body
problems.source_quote: ἵνα μὴ ἐνδυσάμενοι τὸ σῶμα γυμνοὶ εὑρεθῶμεν
problems.why: Greek says 'lest having put on the body we be found naked', not 'when we have put on'
problems.fix: so that when we are clothed with the body we may not be found naked
problems.ruling: Greek ἵνα μὴ … εὑρεθῶμεν = purpose clause, not temporal ‘when’

problems.quote: For what a person has now, that same thing comes forth
problems.source_quote: Ὅπερ γὰρ ἔχει νῦν, αὐτὸ προέρχεται ἔξωθεν τοῦ σώματος τότε
problems.why: Missing 'outside the body' specification; 'comes forth' alone loses the 'from outside' direction
problems.fix: For what a person has now, that same thing comes forth outside the body then
problems.ruling: Greek ἔξωθεν τοῦ σώματος = ‘from outside the body’; English omits this phrase

problems.quote: through the Spirit of the Godhead
problems.why: 'through' is wrong preposition; Greek 'εἰς αὐτοὺς τὸ Πνῦμα... γίνεται' means 'the Spirit becomes/is given to them', not 'through'
problems.fix: the Spirit of the Godhead becomes theirs
problems.ruling: Greek εἰς αὐτοὺς … γίνεται = ‘the Spirit becomes to them’, not ‘through’

problems.quote: so that when we are clothed with the body we may not be found naked
problems.source_quote: ἵνα μὴ ἐνδυσάμενοι τὸ σῶμα γυμνοὶ εὗρεθῶμεν
problems.why: Negates the condition; source says we will be naked if we do not clothe the body.
problems.fix: so that, not having clothed the body, we may be found naked

edits.old: so that when we are clothed with the body we may not be found naked
edits.new: so that, not having clothed the body, we may be found naked

fixed: The English negated the condition: the source says we will be found naked if we have not clothed the body, not that we may not be found naked when clothed. Fixed to 'so that, not having clothed the body, we may be found naked'.

Same month introduced as 'Xanthicus' in intro but never named that in text; reader may think two different months
problems.fix: Include 'Xanthicus' in section 6 or standardize to 'April' in intro

problems.quote: Not even Solomon in all his glory was arrayed like one of these
problems.why: Quoted as 'the Lord said' but this is Jesus speaking in Matthew/Luke; attribution is technically correct but could confuse

problems.quote: so that, not having clothed the body, we may be found naked
problems.why: Double negative logic reversed: means 'so we are NOT found naked' but reads as 'so we may be found naked'
problems.fix: so that, having clothed the body, we may not be found naked

problems.quote: the month called April, the month called April

problems.quote: That Spirit will then be to them garment, food, drink, exultation, joy, peace, clothing, and eternal life
problems.why: 'clothing' and 'garment' are redundant; may be doublet from two Greek synonyms

Citations are correct but the quotation 'Not even Solomon in all his glory was arrayed like one of these' matches neither exactly; Matthew has 'arrayed like one of these' but Luke has 'dressed like one of these'
problems.fix: Note slight variation from Luke's wording

problems.quote: so that, not having clothed the body, we may be found naked
problems.why: Logic is inverted: the goal is to acquire the garment so one is NOT naked; 'not having clothed' contradicts the intent.
problems.fix: Likely 'so that, having clothed the body, we may not be found naked.'

problems.quote: the month called April, the month called April, which is the day of the resurrection
problems.why: Repeats 'the month called April' twice and calls a month 'the day,' conflating month and day.
problems.fix: Remove duplicate phrase; clarify that the month symbolizes the resurrection day.

problems.quote: the flowers of the grass in that season come forth from within the bosoms of the earth
problems.why: 'Bosoms of the earth' is an odd literal rendering; English readers expect 'bosom' for a person, not soil.
problems.fix: Use 'from within the earth' or 'from the earth's depths.'

fixed: The double negative in 'so that, not having clothed the body, we may be found naked' does invert the source's meaning: the source says 'ἵνα μὴ ἐνδυσάμενοι τὸ σῶμα γυμνοὶ εὑρεθῶμεν' (so that, having put on the body, we may not be found naked). Fixed.
The repetition 'the month called April, the month called April' is a dittography in the English; the source has 'Ξανθικὸς, ὁ καλούμενος ᾿Απρίλλιος' once. Fixed by removing the duplicate.

The source has 'ἔνδυμα, βρῶσις, πόσις, ἀγαλλίασις, χαρὰ, εἰρήνη, ἅμφιον, ζωὴ αἰώνιος' — 'ἔνδυμα' and 'ἅμφιον' are near-synonyms both meaning garment/clothing. Rendering both as 'garment' and 'clothing' is redundant in English. Fixed by removing 'clothing'.

The source has 'ἔνδοθεν ἐκ τῶν κόλπων τῆς γῆς' (from within from the bosoms of the earth). 'Bosoms of the earth' is a literal rendering that is odd in English; 'from within the earth' preserves the sense without the awkward image. Fixed.
The glossary problem about 'conduct' is not a real issue: the source uses 'πολιτείας' once, rendered as 'conduct' in the English, which is consistent. No edit needed.

The glossary problem about 'Xanthicus' is not a real issue: the work brief's names field specifies 'Xanthicus': 'the month called April', and the English uses 'the month called April' consistently. No edit needed.
The speaker problem about 'the Lord said' is not a real issue: the source has 'ὁ Κύριος εἶπεν' (the Lord said), and the English renders it as 'the Lord said'. No edit needed.
The scripture problem about the quotation is not a real issue: the English quotation matches the source's Greek, and the citations are correct. No edit needed.

fixed.quote: through the power of the Holy Spirit
fixed.fix: through the ineffable light that is in them even now, that is, through the power of the Holy Spirit
fixed.note: The English drops the light now dwelling in them, which the source names as the Spirit's power.

dismissed.quote: there may be nothing to glorify our flesh
dismissed.why: Greek says 'there is nothing that will glorify our flesh,' not 'nothing to glorify our flesh' as if lacking means; it means no glory will be present.
dismissed.note: 'There may be nothing to glorify our flesh' fairly renders οὐκ ἔστιν ὃ δοξάσει. Separately, the preceding clause wrongly reverses the purpose of ἵνα μὴ ... γυμνοὶ εὑρεθῶμεν and needs its own fix.
